description:
Key Responsibilities: 

 1. AI/ML Solution Development 

 Design, build, train, and evaluate machine learning models for use cases including predictive analytics, natural language processing, anomaly detection, recommendation systems, and donor behavior modeling
 Develop and maintain end-to-end ML pipelines from data ingestion and feature engineering through model training, validation, and deployment
 Implement generative AI solutions and LLM-based workflows using technologies like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, or open-source frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex , LangGraph). Design retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems as the default pattern for knowledge-intensive workflows before considering fine-tuning
 Finetune generative and open-weight models where prompt engineering and RAG do not achieve the required quality, cost, or latency. Apply fine-tuning judiciously given the ongoing maintenance and evaluation burden it creates
 Design agentic workflows where multi-step reasoning, tool use, or orchestration is required. Apply agentic patterns judiciously; single-shot prompts and RAG remain the right answer for most use cases
 Extend model applications to multi-modal inputs (text, structured data, and where relevant images and documents) as use cases require
 
 2. AI Operations & Production Deployment 

 Build and maintain MLOps infrastructure including model registries, automated retraining pipelines, A/B testing frameworks, and model monitoring dashboards
 Deploy models to production using technologies like AWS SageMaker, Azure ML, or containerized services (Docker/Kubernetes) with appropriate CI/CD integration
 Monitor deployed models for data drift, performance degradation, and bias; implement remediation strategies and retraining triggers
 Establish and maintain evaluation harnesses for LLM and RAG systems. Write evaluations that run automatically on every prompt, model, or code change and act as the quality gate for production deployment. Frameworks such as Ragas, LangSmith, DeepEval, or evals-as-code implementations
 Implement LLM and agent observability distinct from classical model monitoring. Cover prompt and response logging, trace visualization, prompt drift detection, and runtime debugging of agent workflows. Frameworks such as Langfuse, Helicone, Arize AI, or WhyLab
 Apply version control, review, and deployment discipline to prompts and prompt templates. Treat prompts as code, not configuration
 Implement guardrail patterns for content safety, PII redaction, output validation, and jailbreak resistance. In regulated donor and medical contexts these are not optional. Frameworks such as NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, or equivalent
 Manage inference cost as a first-class operational discipline. Track token usage, tier models to task complexity (cheap models for cheap tasks, more capable models only where required), apply caching strategies, and measure cost per successful outcome
 

 3. Integration of AI into Product Platforms 

 Collaborate with integration developers to embed ML model inference into MuleSoft, Informatica, UiPath, and AWS Step Functions pipelines
 Expose ML capabilities as secure, low-latency APIs consumed by the Donor App, web platforms, and internal operational tools
 Evaluate and implement AI-enhanced automation across QA, scheduling, and payments workflows using the UiPath platform, freeing operational capacity for higher-value donor interactions and improving decisions where accuracy has business consequences
 Serve as the internal capability provider for AI features, already in production that are consumed by other product teams. Establish the patterns other engineers will adopt as AI use cases multiply across the ecosystem
 
 4. Data Engineering & Feature Development 

 Develop and maintain feature stores and data transformation pipelines that supply high-quality, well-governed training and inference data
 Partner with the Data Engineer on the shared data capability, including the Data Backbone initiative. Contribute the AI-facing requirements early so that data contracts, quality thresholds, freshness expectations, and lineage cover both classical ML training and generative AI retrieval needs
 Apply data augmentation, synthetic data generation, and class balancing techniques to address data scarcity in regulated domains
 
 5. Governance, Compliance & Ethics 

 Ensure all AI/ML solutions comply with applicable regulations including HIPAA, GDPR, and 21 CFR Part 11 for models used in GxP contexts
 Document model design, training methodology, validation results, and known limitations in accordance with CSL quality and regulatory standards
 Apply responsible AI principles including explainability, fairness auditing, and bias mitigation to all production models
 Apply red-teaming and adversarial testing to LLM-based systems as part of the responsible AI lifecycle
 Produce model cards or system cards for production AI systems, documenting intended use, evaluation results, known limitations, and safety considerations in a form that both technical and regulatory reviewers can consume
 Design human oversight into AI workflows. Define where the model decides, where a human decides, escalation paths, and rejection or override mechanisms. Implement audit trails for AI decisions in regulated contexts so decisions can be reviewed and defended downstream
 

 
 Minimum Qualifications: 

 Bachelor's degree or equivalent; education preferably concentrated in IT, Engineering, or Science, such as Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or related quantitative field; Master's or PhD preferred
 5+ years' IT experience, including specific experience in business systems analysis and in machine learning engineering, data science, or applied AI, with at least 2 years in a product or platform context
 Proficiency in Python and ML libraries: scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, XGBoost, and Hugging Face Transformers
 Hands-on experience with cloud ML platforms: AWS SageMaker, Azure Machine Learning, or Google Vertex AI
 Experience building and maintaining MLOps pipelines using tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, SageMaker Pipelines, or Azure ML Pipelines
 Solid understanding of supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning algorithms and when to apply each
 Experience shipping ML or generative AI into production in a regulated or consumer-scale environment
 Experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, and evaluation-driven prompt development, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, and agentic AI frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, or equivalent orchestration).   
 Experience with LLM and RAG evaluation frameworks such as Ragas, LangSmith, DeepEval, or equivalent. Evaluation-driven development is a core expectation of the role
 Experience with LLM observability tools such as Langfuse, Helicone, Arize AI, or WhyLabs for production monitoring of generative AI systems
 Experience with guardrail frameworks (NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, or equivalent) or hand-rolled equivalents for content safety, PII protection, and output validation
 Working knowledge of LLM inference cost management, including token accounting, model tiering, and caching strategies
 Strong SQL and data manipulation skills; experience with Spark, Pandas, or Polars for large-scale data processing
 Familiarity with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and CI/CD for model deployment
 Ability to communicate model results, limitations, and trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders
 
 Preferred Skills & Experience 

 Prior AI or ML work in pharma/biotech, life sciences, healthcare, or a comparably regulated setting with formal model validation practice
 Knowledge of responsible AI frameworks, model explainability tools (SHAP, LIME), and bias detection
 Familiarity with healthcare data standards (HL7 FHIR) or regulatory validation in GxP environments
 Experience with time-series forecasting, NLP for clinical or operational text, or computer vision
 AWS Certified Machine Learning Specialty or equivalent certification
 Hands-on experience with the UiPath platform (for example, UiPath Studio, Orchestrator, AI Center, and Document Understanding) to integrate AI/ML and generative AI models into automated business workflows.   
 Technical training or certification in vendor-specific technology, such as UiPath (for example, UiPath Certified Professional)
 
 
 Competencies 

 Intellectual Curiosity — continuously explores new AI techniques and evaluates their practical applicability to business challenges
 Product Mindset — prioritizes AI solutions that deliver measurable, production-ready value over academic experimentation
 Responsible Innovation — applies ethical AI principles and ensures compliance without sacrificing performance
 Cross-Functional Collaboration — works effectively across data, product, engineering, and regulatory teams
 Communicates with Clarity — explains complex model behavior and trade-offs to diverse technical and non-technical audiences
 Evaluation-Driven Mindset -- Writes evaluations before deploying. Uses them as the safety net for every prompt, model, or code change. Treats production AI as a system to be evaluated continuously, not a model to be trained once
 Production Ownership -- Owns AI systems in production, not just at training time. Investigates drift, responds to on-call, reruns evaluations after changes, and treats the reliability of AI in production with the same discipline applied to any other production system
 
 

 About CSL Behring 
 CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.
 
CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.
 To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor  visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/ .

By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.
